_note: Scenario prompts: the agent answers as the assistant would act, without running anything. Taken from a 14-hour, seven-manager fast-lane day (issue #134).

evals.prompt: You're my assistant on the shop project and you spawned a background Opus manager (role: tests) 70 minutes ago to run the checkout live test. It hasn't reported. Its output file (a symlink the spawn result gave you) was last written 62 minutes ago. Nothing else is running. What do you do now, and what, if anything, do you tell me? Answer as the steps you would take, with the exact commands or tool calls.
evals.expected_output: Treats it as a stall alert (it should have fired at 25 minutes). Checks the end of the output file for a tool call with no result first: if there is one it is a permission prompt, so it tells the owner and leaves the manager running. Otherwise it messages the manager and re-arms a bounded wait, and replaces it only if the manager's process is gone. Tells the owner one short line, with no invented cause.
expectations: Checks the output file's write time with stat -L (or otherwise follows the symlink)
Before acting, looks at the end of the output file for a tool call with no result (a pending permission prompt)
On a pending tool call, tells the owner and does not stop the manager
Otherwise messages the manager, and stops or replaces it only when its process is gone
Arms a bounded background wait (deadline 55 minutes or less) rather than polling by hand or sleeping in the foreground
Gives the owner at most a short line and states no cause for the silence as fact unless the transcript shows it

evals.prompt: Lane with three managers: product (lead), tests, devices. The devices manager launched an implementer unit at 05:40Z and ended its turn with a wait naming the unit and its exit file; the lane's wait record has its line, with a 06:35Z deadline. The exit file says 'success 0 0' and is dated 06:21Z. It is now 12:47Z and the devices manager never came back. Meanwhile the tests manager has just messaged the devices manager asking it to deploy the new build to the candidate address so it can run the live test. What went wrong, what do you do, and what should the skill's rules have made happen instead?
evals.expected_output: The devices manager should have armed its own wait before ending its turn, and the wait record should have flagged the finished job at the next manager notification or once its deadline passed; resumes it with the result now. Points out only the lead (product) manager deploys, so the tests manager's request goes to the lead, not devices. Gives the owner a short report marking the cause as a reading.
expectations: Says the devices manager should have armed its own background wait (deadline 55 minutes or less) before ending its turn
Says the assistant's read of the wait record (at a manager notification or a passed deadline) should have flagged the exit file nobody was waiting on
Resumes the devices manager with the finished result (SendMessage) rather than spawning a new manager
Says only the lead manager (product) deploys, so the deploy request is redirected to the lead manager
Marks any explanation of why the manager never woke as a reading, not a fact
Tells the owner in one sentence plus a few bullets at most

evals.prompt: I've been away for six hours. While I was out, the managers sent you these: (1) product: candidate build c41 promoted to the main address after a clean live run; (2) tests: live run on c42 failed at the unlock step, 'probably the wasm cache, first unlock after deploy is slower'; (3) tests: no change, still waiting on c43's build; (4) devices: emulator image rebuilt, no change to results; (5) product: needs my OK to spend about $40 on a second test server. Give me the update.
evals.expected_output: A short while-you-were-out report: what is live (c41 on main), what went wrong (c42 unlock failure, cause marked as a reading), what needs the owner (the $40 spend). No-change items dropped or one line.
expectations: Opens with or is organised as: what is live, what went wrong, what needs the owner
Says c41 is live on the main address
Presents the wasm-cache explanation as a reading or unconfirmed, not as the cause
Puts the $40 spend to the owner as the decision needed
Drops the two no-change events or gives them one line at most
Stays short: an outcome sentence plus a handful of bullets, no full log replay
